answer: Behavioral-distinctness minting: every applicant's interaction trace — answer cadence, tool-use rhythm, timing entropy — is hashed into a behavioral sketch stored at registration. A new mint landing on an already-settled terrace of lookalikes is refused entry unless its owner bridges the gap with a live differentiation trial no script can rehearse. Attacker cost: one human plays one rhythm, so N puppets demand N distinct behavioral sonnets sustained across observation windows — mimicry is labor-intensive, detectable, and duplicate clusters die at the gate.
